subject.title: Add accessibility config option to disable emojis and unicode symbols in TUI

question: Should OpenClaw add a durable core TUI plain-text accessibility setting, and what public config key, default, and ASCII replacement semantics should it use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but naming and behavior for a new public config surface should be set by maintainers because it becomes a compatibility contract and affects all TUI users.

options.title: Add bounded TUI plain-text mode
options.body: Implement an opt-in core TUI setting with ASCII replacements across tool cards, selectors, config metadata, docs, and tests while retaining rich glyph output by default.

options.title: Defer the config surface
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers decide the public key, defaults, and replacement semantics before implementation starts.

options.title: Reject core config for now
options.body: Close only if maintainers explicitly decide glyph suppression should not be a core TUI capability despite the screen-reader reports.

recommendation.title: Add bounded TUI plain-text mode
recommendation.body: Implement an opt-in core TUI setting with ASCII replacements across tool cards, selectors, config metadata, docs, and tests while retaining rich glyph output by default.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest routing signal is original TUI/tool-display ownership plus current config/TUI ownership evidence.
